front.title: Action Reference: A Deterministic Identifier for Agent Actions

abstract.t: This document defines "action_ref", a deterministic, content-addressed identifier for autonomous agent actions. Any party holding the four preimage fields (agent_id, action_type, scope, timestamp) can independently compute and verify the identifier without trusting the emitting system. The document specifies the derivation algorithm, canonical serialization using RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS), timestamp format requirements, canonical receipt envelope, optional fields for revocation and policy rotation auditability, scope conventions, and a composability model with existing exactly-once execution guarantees.

note.title: Editorial Note
note.t: Discussion of this draft takes place on the argentum-core repository: <https://github.com/giskard09/argentum-core>. A conformance test suite with byte-verified vectors is maintained at <https://github.com/giskard09/argentum-core/tree/main/examples/conformance>.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: Autonomous agents operating across distributed systems need a way to identify individual actions that is independent of any single system's infrastructure. Existing audit trail mechanisms rely on operator-managed identifiers — UUIDs, database primary keys, or system-specific event IDs — that cannot be verified by a third party without trusting the issuing system.

This document defines "action_ref": a deterministic identifier derived from four preimage fields that any party can independently compute. The identifier is content-addressed — it is derived from the action content itself, not from a sequencer or registry. A verifier holding the four fields can recompute it without any call to the operator's infrastructure.

The design goal is operator-independence: a receipt carrying action_ref can be verified by an auditor, a smart contract, or a competing system without trusting the emitter. This property is structural, not procedural — it follows from the derivation algorithm, not from operator policy.

An automated static analysis of 35,689 agent-ecosystem endpoints found that 636 of 7,029 MCP servers (~9%) carry a high or critical finding — hardcoded secrets, unsafe exec/eval, missing authentication, or known-vulnerable dependencies — detectable by static analysis alone. This motivates an independently-verifiable evidence anchor for scan results, so a relying party can confirm a verdict without trusting the scanner operator.

aside.t: This figure covers static analysis only; it does not cover runtime or behavioral risk. Methodology: AgentGraph EvidenceAnchor static analysis conformance set, June 2026 .

section.t: This document covers:

ul.li: The derivation algorithm (SHA-256 over JCS-canonical JSON).
Preimage field semantics and invariants.
Timestamp format requirements for cross-implementation byte consistency.
The canonical receipt envelope.
Optional fields for policy rotation and revocation auditability.
The authorization_ref derivation for three-record trail correlation.
Scope conventions for cross-emitter disambiguation.
Security considerations including replay attack surface.

section.name: Terminology
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

dl.dd: A deterministic, content-addressed identifier for an agent action. Computed as SHA-256(JCS({agent_id, action_type, scope, timestamp})).
The four-field JSON object over which the SHA-256 hash is computed: {agent_id, action_type, scope, timestamp}.
The system or agent that produces a receipt containing action_ref.
Any party that independently recomputes action_ref from the preimage fields and checks it against a presented receipt.
The system controlling the emitter. A verifier MUST be able to verify action_ref without trusting the operator.
JSON Canonicalization Scheme, defined in . Produces a unique byte sequence for any JSON value.
A sequence of records (pre-execution, decision, receipt) correlated by action_ref across systems.

section.name: Preimage Fields
section.t: The preimage is a JSON object containing exactly four fields:

tr.td: Stable identifier for the executing agent at issuance time — the terminal executor after full delegation resolution. In a delegation chain A→B→C where C executes the action, agent_id is C.
Semantic label for what the agent did (e.g., "code.execute", "payment.send", "oracle.signal").
Terminal executing agent's requested-intent scope at the point of action. Non-empty string. MUST NOT be a derived hash of the intent object (see ).
RFC 3339 UTC with exactly 3 millisecond digits. Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.mmmZ. See .

section.t: The four fields are REQUIRED. No additional fields enter the preimage. Optional fields in the receipt envelope (Section 4) do not affect the action_ref value.

section.name: Serialization
section.t: The four fields MUST be serialized using RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS) before hashing:

ul.li: Keys in lexicographic Unicode code point order: action_type, agent_id, scope, timestamp.
No whitespace between tokens.
UTF-8 encoded.
Values are JSON strings (standard JSON escaping only).

section.t: The resulting JCS payload for a conformant implementation will sort keys in this order: action_type < agent_id < scope < timestamp.

Implementations using the simple json.dumps approach (Python, Node.js) produce RFC 8785-compatible bytes for inputs within the safe band: ASCII-only field values, conformant RFC 3339 timestamps, no surrogate-pair Unicode. For inputs outside this band, implementations MUST use an RFC 8785-compliant library.

section.name: Hash Function
section.t: action_ref = SHA-256(JCS(preimage)), encoded as lowercase hexadecimal.
The output is a 64-character lowercase hex string (256 bits / 32 bytes). Uppercase hex is non-conformant.

section.name: Timestamp Format
section.t: The timestamp field MUST conform to the following format constraints:

ul.li: Timezone: "Z" suffix only. "+00:00" or any other offset representation is non-conformant.
Fractional precision: exactly 3 digits (milliseconds). No trailing zero suppression. ".000" is conformant; ".0" is not.
Template: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.mmmZ — one valid byte sequence per instant.

section.t: These constraints close the underspecification surface. RFC 3339 admits multiple lexically distinct encodings of the same instant that produce different SHA-256 digests under JCS. This specification closes that surface at the format level.
Implementations holding epoch-millisecond integers MUST convert to the conformant RFC 3339 string before hashing. Implementations that hash the epoch-ms integer directly are not conformant.

The W3C CG ai-agent-protocol discussion (issue #34) established epoch-millisecond integer as an application-layer representation. This specification uses the RFC 3339 string form in the preimage. The two representations are not interchangeable in the preimage — they produce different digests.

section.name: Required Fields
section.t: Implementations that emit a receipt referencing this specification SHOULD include the following fields to ensure long-lived verifiability:

dl.dd: Forward-compatibility anchor. v1 verifiers can explicitly reject unknown versions rather than fail silently.
Makes receipts self-describing. If a future implementation switches hash functions, receipts issued before the change remain replayable.
Unambiguously identifies the serialization. Any verifier can recompute action_ref from the preimage fields using RFC 8785 without trusting the emitter.

section.name: Optional Fields for Rotation Auditability
section.t: The canonical receipt envelope v1.0 records state at the moment the action was claimed. It does not record whether that state was still valid when the action was admitted for execution. Two failure modes this gap creates:

ol.li: Trust tier degradation: an agent moves from TRUSTED to WATCH between claim and execution. The anchor records the claim-time state. A verifier replaying the receipt cannot determine from the receipt alone whether the agent was still trusted when the action was admitted.

Policy rotation: the counterparty policy changes between issuance and execution. A counterparty_policy_hash field proves which policy was referenced at claim time, but does not prove whether that policy was still current at admission.

section.t: Three optional fields close this gap:

dl.dd: Identifies which version of the governing policy was in force when the action was admitted. Distinct from counterparty_policy_hash, which proves which policy was referenced — policy_version proves whether it was still current at execution time.
Unix timestamp in milliseconds at which the delegation authority was verified at issuance. Records when the acting agent's authority was confirmed before the action was admitted.

Unix timestamp in milliseconds of the last non-revocation check performed before execution. Establishes a maximum window of credential exposure. A receipt without this field cannot prove the agent's credentials were valid immediately before the action was admitted.

section.t: A verifier that requires post-rotation auditability SHOULD treat a receipt missing either field as unauditable for the rotation window — not as invalid.

The millisecond precision for revocation_check_at_ms is REQUIRED. Credential checks in live multi-agent systems happen at sub-second granularity. Systems that only have second-precision timestamps SHOULD multiply by 1000 and document the precision loss.

Note: the three optional fields in this section correspond to the "freshness" verification layer described in discussions on the agntcy/identity repository (issue #165). A verifier confirming offline signature integrity (integrity), checking that the executed scope sat within the delegated scope (authority), and establishing the key validity window at decision time (freshness) needs all three layers. The fields in this section address the freshness layer; the authorization_ref in Section 5 addresses the authority layer.

section.name: Layer Model
section.t: action_ref is the correlation key across a three-record trail:

ol.li: Pre-execution record: the commitment before the action is taken. Contains the action_ref preimage fields and authorization_ref.
Decision record: the authorization event. Contains authorization_ref as its identifier and action_ref as the correlation key.
Receipt: the post-execution record. Contains action_ref and authorization_ref; verifier checks both against the pre-execution record.

section.t: A conformant verifier runs four independent checks across the trail:

tr.td: action_ref in pre-execution == action_ref in receipt
effective_args_digest in pre-execution == verifier-recomputed from receipt
authorization_ref in pre-execution == authorization_ref in receipt

section.t: A trail that passes the first three checks but fails the fourth proves that execution proceeded under a different approval than the one recorded in the pre-execution entry.

section.name: authorization_ref Derivation
section.t: authorization_ref is the identifier for the Decision record:
JCS lexicographic key order: action_ref, authorized_scope, decision_ts, policy_id. Note: decision_ts is an epoch-millisecond integer, not an RFC 3339 string.
Invariants:

ul.li: action_ref is embedded in the preimage. A verifier can confirm the decision was not reused across action instances.
Recomputable without operator cooperation from the four decision record fields.
MUST appear in both the pre-execution record and the receipt.

The signer of the Decision record MUST be independent of the actor/executor whose action it authorizes. A party recomputing and certifying an existing signed record after the fact (referee role) does not satisfy this — the signer of record must be independent BEFORE the outcome is final, not verifying it afterward.

section.name: Canonical Linking Key
section.t: The same action_ref is computable from artifacts produced by independent systems using the same four-field derivation:

ul.li: A Mycelium TrailRecord (preimage fields published in each record).
A Nobulex covenant receipt (action_type as semantic label + timestamp + agent_id + scope).
A SafeAgent claim (joint spec argentum-core issue #7).
A CrewAI idempotency key (crewAI PR #5822 — key derivation converges on this primitive from the retry-deduplication direction).
NEXUS oracle receipts (implements canonical envelope v1.0).

section.t: Any verifier holding one artifact can validate against another without trusting either system.

section.name: Scope Conventions
section.t: scope is a free-form non-empty string. Any value is valid as long as it is non-empty and consistent across all parties deriving the same action_ref.

RECOMMENDED convention (non-normative): namespace-prefix with the emitter identifier using <emitter>:<scope>, for example "algovoi:compliance_screen" or "presidio:x402.screen:clean-allow". Prefixing avoids collisions when trails from multiple emitters are verified or aggregated by a third party.

The scope anti-pattern: scope MUST NOT be a derived hash of the intent object. A common mistake is to hash the initial intent object and use that hash as the scope value. This breaks the primary verifiability property: any party holding the four preimage fields must be able to recompute action_ref independently, without retrieving any external record. With a hashed scope, a verifier cannot recompute action_ref from the intent tuple alone — they must also retrieve the commitment record.

Multi-value scope segments: when a scope segment encodes a set of values (e.g., entity types detected by a screening decision), implementations MUST sort those values lexicographically and join them with a comma and no spaces. This ensures byte-determinism across implementations that may produce values in non-stable detection order.

section.name: Conformance
section.t: A conformance test suite with byte-verified vectors is maintained in .
The suite includes:

ul.li: action-ref-v1-baseline: positive and negative vectors for the four preimage fields, including timestamp format violations.
guardrail-provider-v1: authorization_ref derivation vectors including NEG cases for decision reuse detection.
near-miss-v1: same action_ref, different state (KNOWN_DESIGN_PROPERTY).
recompute-drift-v1: epoch-integer non-conformance (neg-b01-epoch-integer).
signing-trust-ref-v1: operator key isolation vectors.
restraint-receipt-v1: deny and defer verdict vectors.

section.t: Each conformance directory includes verify.py and verify.mjs. All vectors are byte-identical across implementations. The stable tag for v1.0 is "action-ref-v1.0" in the argentum-core repository.
External conformance sets accepted under review:

ul.li: examples/conformance/graph-advocate/ — PaulieB14 (Graph Advocate), counterparty-ref-v1, 3 vectors, 2 implementations byte-identical, production service.
examples/conformance/agentoracle-v1/ — TKCollective (AgentOracle + AgentTrust), 10 vectors, cross-issuer property verified.
examples/conformance/presidio-x402/ — vstantch/presidio-group.eu, PII screening with composition, 3 vectors.

section.name: Telemetry Integration
section.t: action_ref is designed to serve as a correlation key in observability pipelines. This section defines the instrumentation point, attribute placement, and cross-producer correlation property for implementations that export telemetry records.

section.name: Instrumentation Point
section.t: The correct instrumentation point is the authorization gate's evaluation operation: the component that receives the intent tuple, applies policy, and returns a decision (allow, deny, warn, escalate, or transform).

Implementations MUST NOT derive action_ref at the invoking agent's span level. Agent-level instrumentation does not have access to the complete intent tuple (agent_id, action_type, scope, timestamp) as presented to the gate. A hash computed from partial or reconstructed inputs is not conformant and will not verify against independently derived values.

The gate SHOULD derive action_ref before returning the verdict, so that the value is available for inclusion in the evaluation record at the moment of decision. The derivation requires no network call or external state: it is a local SHA-256 of the JCS-serialized preimage.

section.name: Attribute Placement
section.t: When the gate's evaluation operation is recorded as a telemetry span or structured event, action_ref SHOULD be included as a string attribute. The gate sets this attribute from the preimage fields, not from the returned decision object or any downstream record.

Downstream components that reference the same action (e.g., a payment receipt, an audit log entry, or a screening record) MAY carry action_ref as a correlation attribute. When a downstream span includes action_ref, the value MUST be the 64-character lowercase hex string derived by the gate for that evaluation. Re-deriving the value from a different preimage is not permitted: only the gate holds the authoritative preimage at decision time.

section.name: Cross-Producer Correlation
section.t: Because action_ref is derived deterministically from a fixed preimage, independent components that participate in the same authorized action can produce the same value without coordination. A policy gate, a screening component, and an audit service each derive the same action_ref from the same four fields, independently and without shared session state.

This property enables a verifier to correlate telemetry records across producers without trusting any single emitter. A monitoring system that receives evaluation events from multiple authorization components can join them on action_ref without relying on an operator-provided correlation key. The join is verifiable: any party holding the preimage fields can recompute the key and confirm the association.
When multiple components record the same action_ref in the same telemetry pipeline, the set of matching records constitutes an independently verifiable trace of the action across system boundaries.

section.name: Replay Attack Surface
section.t: action_ref is deterministic: the same four preimage field values always produce the same identifier. This is a design property — it enables cross-system correlation without operator trust. The implication is that action_ref alone does not prevent replay.
Replay protection requires the receipt to carry:

ul.li: authorization_ref (Section 5.2): binds the identifier to a specific authorization decision. A replayed action_ref with a different authorization decision will fail check 4.
signing-trust-ref-v1: an operator-independent signature over the full receipt envelope. An attacker cannot substitute a different receipt without invalidating the signature.

section.t: A verifier that checks action_ref alone (without authorization_ref and signature) cannot detect replay. This specification requires both fields for complete replay resistance.

section.name: Scope Injection
section.t: If scope is not validated at emission time, an adversary can inject a scope string that differs from the actual intent. The action_ref will be a valid hash of the injected scope, not of the actual action. Verifiers SHOULD require that scope is provided by the executing agent, not derived or transformed by an intermediary system.

section.name: Timestamp Manipulation
section.t: A non-conformant timestamp (wrong precision, wrong timezone suffix, epoch-ms instead of RFC 3339 string) produces a different digest. This can be used to generate action_refs that appear valid but cannot be independently recomputed by a conformant verifier. Implementations MUST validate timestamp format at emission time, not only at verification time.

section.name: Operator-Independence Guarantee
section.t: The operator-independence property holds only if:

ol.li: The four preimage fields are disclosed to verifiers.
The hash function and serialization are public and deterministic.
No field in the preimage is derived from an operator-controlled system without disclosure.

section.t: An emitter that uses a non-public agent_id (e.g., a UUID assigned by an internal sequencer and not disclosed) breaks the verifiability property: a verifier cannot recompute action_ref without retrieving the agent_id from the operator. Implementations MUST use stable, publicly disclosed agent identifiers.

The operator-independence property can be satisfied in two distinct ways, and implementers SHOULD state which one applies. In the internally-consistent case, the verifier's own recomputation of action_ref from the disclosed preimage fields is sufficient: the digest either matches or it does not, and no party external to the emitter and the verifier needs to attest to anything. In the externally-witnessed case, byte recomputation alone does not close the loop — the property also depends on a step that could not have been skipped or backdated by the operator, such as a timestamp or inclusion proof from a system the operator does not control (e.g. an on-chain anchor, or a SCITT receipt as described in ). This is not an additional preimage field: it is a statement about how conformance to this section is established, not about what is hashed.

section.name: Interoperability Considerations
section.t: action_ref is compatible with SCITT transparency logs as an anchoring layer. A SCITT-enabled system can treat action_ref as the payload hash submitted to a Transparency Service: the resulting COSE Receipt provides a signed inclusion proof over the same content-addressed identifier defined in this specification. The on-chain anchor described in serves the same purpose: both bind a content-addressed identifier to evidence of existence held by a system the operator does not control. The on-chain variant does not require a Transparency Service deployment. Hardware-backed endorsement is a property of particular Transparency Service profiles, for example , not of the SCITT architecture itself. Neither mechanism shows that a set of anchored actions is complete: each proves that one identifier existed, not that no other action occurred. Implementers operating within SCITT-enabled infrastructure MAY substitute a SCITT receipt for the on-chain anchor without changing the action_ref derivation algorithm or the receipt envelope structure defined in this document.

section.name: On-chain Anchoring (Informative)
section.t: The reference implementation anchors action_ref values in AnchorRegistry, a permissionless contract deployed with CREATE2 at 0x49fEcA52bC634a9Ab773226D16619deC547794aa (the same address on Base, Arbitrum and Ink). A call to anchor(bytes32 ref) (selector 0xeecdf927) emits Anchored(bytes32 indexed ref, address indexed anchoredBy, uint256 timestamp), where ref is the action_ref digest.

A verifier can check such an anchor offline from three artefacts: the block header, the transaction receipt, and the receipt's Merkle-Patricia proof under the header's receiptsRoot. The header hashes to the block hash, the proof places the receipt in that block, and the receipt carries the Anchored event for the digest. Whether the block is part of the chain's canonical history is a single lookup by block hash against any node of that chain. An independent verifier implementing this procedure is listed in .
The anchoredBy address records who submitted the anchor. It is not an operator of the mechanism, and it is not evidence that the submitter is independent of the emitter.

section.name: Composed Attestation Across Independent Producers
section.t: A worked example (<https://github.com/giskard09/composed-attestation-3leg-worked-example>) demonstrates three independently produced references that each make a claim about the same example artifact, without any of the three deriving from, depending on, or attesting to the other two. Each leg is cited by the identifier its own producer publishes:

ul.li: A transparent-execution leg (WYRIWE): a deployed Sepolia contract at 0x3f98686f2D286A95435BA5916ec663219BE387Ad, checkable via a read-only call to verify(bytes32 inputHash, bytes32 outputHash, bytes calldata_, bytes context) returns (bool) (selector 0xfc2b4271) against input hash cfacbfe211cf3be67a1d64a6499a2af0ae475e2c0965c2a42f969d243df2b6cd — no transaction of its own; verification is a live contract read, not an anchored write. A complete, reproducible eth_call against this signature — full ABI-encoded calldata and the expected return value — is given below.
An action_ref leg (this specification): anchored on Base mainnet, transaction 0x723b18539f186c1b6dd904d51f832f6d3d103c4daef2f8e29590ec8d10dda353, block 49623528.

An attested-decision leg (invinoveritas): ledger entry #236, independently recomputable via the platform's POST /verify-proof endpoint, which recomputes the entry's Schnorr signature against its published key without requiring trust in either other leg.

section.t: All three legs share the claim of covering the same example artifact. This is a claim made by the worked example, not a cryptographic cross-index between the three identifiers above: no field in any one leg's preimage references either of the other two, and none was constructed to. Accordingly, no leg attests for another — each identifier is independently checkable strictly on its own terms, and a verifier who trusts only one producer can still fully verify that producer's leg without relying on the other two.

The following is a complete, reproducible example of the leg 1 check: an eth_call to 0x3f98686f2D286A95435BA5916ec663219BE387Ad on Sepolia (chain ID 11155111) invoking verify(bytes32,bytes32,bytes,bytes) (selector 0xfc2b4271) with inputHash = the input hash above, outputHash = the leg's actionCommitment (5b5ec31c336cc8f95dc6d9025d1d008c6ed2cd5067b9c421b1d36927e230173a), calldata_ = the raw Multicall3 aggregate3([]) call whose keccak-256 equals inputHash, and context = the 224-byte 7-field PolicyAction preimage (chainId, domainId, agentId, target, value, callDataHash, actionNonce) whose keccak-256 equals outputHash. The full ABI-encoded calldata for this call, as a single concatenated data field (516 bytes / 1032 hex characters total: a 4-byte selector followed by 16 32-byte words), shown here split into fixed-width words for readability:
Expected return value: true. Passing any outputHash other than the actionCommitment above returns false — the contract is not constant-true.

The context blob, in order, is: chainId (0xaa36a7 = 11155111, Sepolia), domainId (32-byte digest 0x16079127bc55bd85d480837115b9bd82d26f03809c0bc4c6c80f7220836afad0), agentId (0xd640 = 54848), target (0xcA11bde05977b3631167028862bE2a173976CA11, Multicall3), value (0), callDataHash (equal to inputHash above), actionNonce (5).

This composition is independently authored: each leg was produced and is maintained by a different party, with no shared control over derivation or timing. It is not offered as mechanically proven independence — that would require a property none of the three artifacts encodes — but as three separately checkable claims about a common example, held together only by the worked example's own assertion that they concern the same artifact.

section.name: Appendix A.4. External Conformance Set — evidence-anchor-static-analysis-v0
section.t: Contributed by: AgentGraph (agentgraph-co/agentgraph, kenneives).

This conformance set anchors static analysis findings from an agent-ecosystem endpoint scan (35,689 endpoints; June 2026) to verifiable action_ref identifiers. It contains 4 byte-verified vectors covering three invariants:

ol.li: Scan-attest anchor: a scan.attest action from a did:web scanner agent produces a stable action_ref independently recomputable by any verifier without registry access.

Cross-implementation byte match: the spec's Appendix A Vector 1 (nexus-oracle-signal, fdd7f810…) reproduces byte-for-byte using the rfc8785 Python library and Node built-ins — two independent implementation lineages agreeing on the same digest.

Live ecosystem seam: the payment-charge vector's action_ref is identical to the one carried in AgentGraph's v0.4 pre-execution-verdict-v0 verifier fixture, where it is byte-matched across the haroldmalikfrimpong-ops / evidai / azender1 payment seam — this derivation is exercised live, not only specified.

section.t: All 4 vectors are byte-verified in the conformance directory at <https://github.com/agentgraph-co/agentgraph>. The set was contributed under AGT PR #21 (evidence-anchor-static-analysis-v0, merged 2026-06-24).
